narrative:
Cost of sales is USD 246.4B in the FY2026 budget — 50.1% of revenue. Crude and product purchases for the downstream system are 52% of it, royalties and production taxes 20%, refining and processing 12%, and lifting cost and shipping 8% each.

Upstream lifting cost is USD 3.25/boe against USD 3.20 in plan; offshore is the only field more than 2% above plan. Royalties are price-linked, so the lower Brent deck reduces cost of sales by about USD 0.4B per USD 1/bbl.

The cost pressure is in freight and refining: VLCC rates are 29% above plan and refining utilities and catalysts 6% above plan after the hydrocracker catalyst change.

signals.title: VLCC freight above plan
signals.excerpt: Arabian Gulf–Asia VLCC rates average $58,000/day versus $45,000 in plan on Red Sea re-routing.

signals.title: Refining margin squeeze at international JVs
signals.excerpt: International Refining JVs run at 68% cost of sales; a $2/bbl drop in the Singapore complex margin costs about $2B of EBITDA.
